entities.summary:
Psychoanalysis is a foundational Psychological theory that was founded in 1890 by the viennese neurologist Sigmund Freud. Born in Moravia, Austria-Hungary, Freud's work revolutionized the field of psychology, introducing the concept of the unconscious mind and the process of free association.

    This groundbreaking theory gained international attention, with Freud's books becoming bestsellers in multiple languages. His ideas influenced many notable figures, including Sigmund Rubinstein and Anna Freud, who continued his work.

    The psychoanalytic movement expanded globally, shaping the way people understood themselves and their relationships. It also spawned numerous offshoots, such as Object Relations Theory and Lacanian psychoanalysis.

    Despite controversy and criticism, psychoanalysis remains a cornerstone of modern psychology, continuing to be studied and applied in various fields, including psychiatry, education, and social work.
